title: Reacting to Something New: ideges, bátorság, nekivág, kihívás

sections.title: The feelings around a first time
sections.content: A first-time story is rarely just the event — it's also how you felt before and during it. Four words help: ideges ("nervous") for how you feel beforehand, bátorság ("courage") for what it took to go ahead anyway, nekivág ("to set out on, to tackle") for the moment you actually start, and kihívás ("challenge") for naming the thing itself.

sections.title: New words for reacting to a first time
rows: to set out on, to tackle

items.spanish: Mielőtt nekivágtam az első nagy kihívásnak, nagyon ideges voltam.
items.english: Before I set out on my first big challenge, I was very nervous.

items.spanish: Sok bátorság kellett hozzá, hogy életemben először egyedül utazzak.
items.english: It took a lot of courage to travel alone for the first time in my life.

sections.content: nekivág takes a dative object, not accusative — nekivágok a kihívásnak ("I set out on the challenge"), not nekivágok a kihívást. Think of neki as literally pointing "at" the thing you're setting out toward, the same logic as odamegy valakinek.
